 Restaurant fire at Houston's Bush Airport sends large plume of smoke into sky
 By Barbi Barbee Houston Updated  October 27, 2026 5:18 PM CDT Published  October 27, 2026 5:03 PM CDT Updated  October 27, 2026 5:18 PM CDT ▾ Restaurant fire at Houston's Bush Airport sends large plume of smoke into sky 
 A restaurant fire sent a large plume of smoke into the sky at Houston's George Bush Intercontinental Airport on Tuesday afternoon, officials say.
 The Brief
 A kitchen fire broke out in Terminal C at Houston's George Bush Intercontinental Airport Tuesday afternoon. 
 Viewer video sent to FOX 26 shows firefighters and a large plume of dark smoke. 
 United Airlines says the fire is not affecting flights. 
 HOUSTON - A restaurant fire sent a large plume of smoke into the sky at Houston's George Bush Intercontinental Airport on Tuesday afternoon, officials say.
 What we know:
 According to the airport, the Houston Fire Department responded to a fire at a restaurant in Terminal C North. Airport officials say passengers in the immediate area were relocated as a precaution.
 According to United Airlines, the fire is not affecting flights.
 Smoke rises over Houston's Bush Airport after restaurant fire 
 A restaurant fire sent a large plume of smoke into the sky at Houston's George Bush Intercontinental Airport on Tuesday afternoon, officials say. Video courtesy: Tom Butt
 Video sent to FOX 26 by a viewer showed firefighters at the airport as a large, dark cloud of smoke rose into the sky.
 What we don't know:
 No further information has been released. We will bring you updates as more information becomes available.
 The Source: The information in this article comes from video of the scene and United Airlines.
